chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have date palms in Basra, so I will sell them and name the price, and reserve the kur (a specific measure/quantity) of dates or more.' He said, 'There is no objection.'
I said, 'May I be your ransom, do we sell the pre-harvest dates (sine)?' He said, 'There is no objection.'
I said, 'May I be your ransom, indeed that is significant with us.'
He said, 'As for if you say that, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted that, but they imposed restrictions upon it. So he (peace be upon him) said,

key_terms.الْكُرّ: A specific measure or quantity of dates

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell date palms and reserve some of the fruit for oneself according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of selling pre-harvest fruits (bay' al-thimar) by distinguishing between the permissibility of reserving a portion (kur) and the general prohibition against selling fruit before its quality becomes evident (badw al-salah). The Imam references the Prophet’s initial allowance of this practice, noting that later restrictions were imposed to prevent injustice (zulm) in transactions, thereby establishing a nuanced legal precedent for commercial dealings in agricultural produce.
